doc.title: Leslie Gourse interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

title: Rowe's own love of jazz
summary: Gourse turns the question on Rowe, who cites Glenn Miller records, Paul Desmond and Cannonball Adderley.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well it’s been fascinating talking to you.
Well thanks a lot. How do you love jazz? How did you come to love jazz?

Whoa — I’m being interviewed all of a sudden. That’s great. That’s a good question. I think it came from my parents. They used to play Glenn Miller records. And that caught my ear and I started out on the clarinet and then switched to saxophone. And there was a few moments along in my life, first of all hearing the Glenn Miller orchestra, although Glenn wasn’t there, but and then hearing Paul Desmond with the Brubeck Quartet on the radio, and then later hearing Cannonball Adderley. Those things made big impressions on

me and that was really the start of it. Interviewing folks like yourself and all the musicians has been really informative for me and for the college here. Because we hope that all our students and visitors to the college will be using this as a way to learn about the history of the music. So thanks for your time.
